attestations.note: The translation of his relics; his principal feast is 11 June. A SECOND RUSSIAN DAY, AND THE ROW WAS NOT MOVED: the 22 апреля ст. ст. day page prints «Апп. Нафанаила , Луки и Климента (I).» and THE FIRST NAME LINK BEHIND THAT LINE IS NAME PAGE 365, «Апостол Варфоломей» — the source identifies Нафанаил with Варфоломей inside its own markup, and both of the lives that page indexes carry «Нафанаил апостол» as a second heading. The identification is stated outright at the end of life1280: «Святители Иоанн Златоуст, Кирилл Александрийский, Епифаний Кипрской и некоторые другие учители Церкви считают апостола Варфоломея за одно лицо с Нафанаилом (Ин. 1, 45-51; Ин. 21, 2)» — so the calendar holds it as the reading of certain Fathers rather than as a bare fact, and it is set out that way in the life. His own pages head four days, «22 апреля , 11 июня , 30 июня (12 ап.) , 25 августа (Перенесение мощей)». One attestation row per church is the schema, so 22 апреля is recorded here and he does not render on it; 11 июня and 30 июня are recorded and NOT READ. THIS IS A ROW SITTING ON A TRANSLATION OF RELICS WHILE THE PRINCIPAL FEAST GOES UNWRITTEN, and it is reported to the author beside `silvanus-of-gaza`, `theodosius-of-the-kyiv-caves` and `job-of-pochaev` rather than resolved here: §4 forbids moving a day. `types` gained `martyr` off life1280, which has him crucified head downwards at Albanopolis, flayed and beheaded. Not checked: azbyka.ru, and the 11 июня, 30 июня and 22 апреля day pages beyond the 22 апреля one read here.

attestations.note: The translation of his relics; his principal feast is 11 June. A SECOND DAY ON THIS CHURCH, ADDED 5 October 2026, AND IT IS §4’S WARNING RUNNING BACKWARDS. **This folder’s `serbian` row stands on the Julian 25 August, and all four of its rows stand on a translation of relics**: the `romanian` row’s own note says «The translation of his relics; his principal feast is 11 June» and the `greek` row’s says the same words. **The Prologue keeps him on the Julian 11 June — the principal day — and one row to a church is the schema, so the principal day has to be recorded as a note on a row that holds the relics’ day.** §4 warns against writing a translation day onto an `undocumented` row because it bars a later reader from the principal one; here the translation day was already venerated when this reader arrived, so **the thing §4 exists to prevent has already happened on this folder, on all four churches, and was not done by this wave.** **NOTHING WAS MOVED, AND THAT IS §4 AND NOT A PREFERENCE.** Changing the day under `replace_venerated` is explicitly not sanctioned and is a question for the report, so the 25 August row is copied back unchanged and this note is added. **IT IS THE AUTHOR’S**, and the shape of the decision is clear: four rows would have to move together, and the three other churches’ notes already say which day they think is the principal one. THE ENTRY IS THE LONGEST OF THE WAVE AND THIS FOLDER IS A 4 kB LIFE BUILT OFF WIKIPEDIA. Its `dates` note cites «Wikipedia’s article “Bartholomew the Apostle”» and Wikidata; **so almost everything the Prologue gives is new to it.** In order: that Bartholomew and Nathanael are by all appearances one and the same person; that he preached with the apostle Philip and with Philip’s sister, the virgin Mariamne, and for a time with John the Theologian, first through Asia, then in India, and last in Armenia; that at Hierapolis the apostles killed by prayer a great serpent the heathen kept and worshipped in a temple; that in the same city they gave sight by prayer to a man who had been forty years blind; that the mob rose and crucified both Philip and Bartholomew, **Bartholomew head downwards**; that an earthquake followed in which the wicked judges and many of the people perished; that many ran to take the apostles down, and Philip had already died while Bartholomew was still alive; that in India he **translated the Gospel of Matthew into the Indian tongue**; that in Armenia he healed the king’s daughter of madness, and the king’s envious brother Astyages took him, crucified him, flayed him and beheaded him at Albanopolis in Armenia; that the Christians buried him in a **lead coffin**, which the heathen threw into the sea because of the wonders at the relics, and the water carried it to the Lipari islands, where the bishop received it on a revelation in a dream and buried it in a church; that he appeared to Joseph the Hymnographer in white robes and blessed him with the Gospel so that he could sing spiritual songs, saying „Нека с језика твога потеку воде небесне мудрости!“; that he appeared to the emperor Anastasius and promised to guard his newly built city of Dara; and that the relics were afterwards carried to Benevento and to Rome. THREE NEW `related` ROWS, ALL RECIPROCAL. `philip-the-apostle` and `mariamne-sister-of-philip`: **the entry narrates one preaching and one crucifixion for Philip and Bartholomew together**, which is the test that owes a row, and Mariamne is named as the third of the company. `joseph-the-hymnographer`: the apostle appears to him, blesses him with the Gospel and speaks a sentence to him, which is a scene and not a citation. `john-the-theologian` is already there and is the fourth companion. **THE MAN HEALED OF BLINDNESS GETS NO ROW AND NO NAME IN THE PROSE.** The entry calls him Стахијe and the corpus holds exactly one Stachys, `stachys-of-byzantium`, the apostle of the Seventy and first bishop of Byzantium — **and nothing in this entry identifies the two**. One Stachys is not two, but neither is one Stachys automatically the other: the object of a healing at Hierapolis is not said here to be a bishop of Byzantium, and a row written on a bare forename and a guess is the failure §3 calls the worst this job has. He is in this note and not in the life. **The bishop of the Lipari islands is named Агатон and gets the same treatment**: eight Agathons and not one of them of Lipari. Astyages, the king, his daughter, the judges and the emperor Anastasius take no rows. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND NOTHING COULD HAVE IMPROVED IT: the folder holds `death` 1st century, and **this entry gives no year for his end at all** — its only dated thing is the reign of Anastasius, centuries later, attached to an apparition. `types` untouched at `apostle`, corroborated by апостол and by „Један од дванаест великих апостола“. No `locations`. **NO SECOND `sr` FORM, AND THAT IS §6.** The folder already stores «Свети апостол Вартоломеј» — **with the rank words inside it**, which is the habit §6 says to leave where it is found and never to copy. This heading would give the bare «Вартоломеј», `foldchk.py` returning `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for it, **but one `sr` form per folder is the rule and a second would be two**. The stored form is left exactly as it is and the contract it breaks is named here rather than mended. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.
